Definition: of foreign origin (H6547); Pharao (i.e. Pharoh), an Egyptian king:--Pharaoh.
BiblicalUsage: Pharaoh is the king of Egypt in the story of Joseph and Moses, and the Greek New Testament names him where the story turns. God gave Joseph favour in the sight of Pharaoh, and Moses was taken up by Pharaoh's daughter, and by faith Moses refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Pharaoh's name stands for the world's power at its highest: a throne, a palace, and a daughter's adoption. Moses walked away from all of it, and Joseph rose above it, because both of them knew a greater King.
RelatedPeople: Pharaoh; Moses; Joseph, Son of Jacob
